full_judgment:
Krishna Debnath, J: This Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure ("Code") has been placed before us for confirmation of the death sentence of condemned-prisoners (1) Md Anwar Hossain @ Shankar Chandra Debnath @ Md Rajib @ Golam Rabbain and (2) Md Jakir Hossain @ Zakir passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Session Case No. 313 of 2005 arising out of GRP Police Station Case No.7 dated 10-4-2005 corresponding to GR No. 20 of 2005 convicting them under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to death. 

 4. The relevant story for disposal of the Prosecution Case, in brief, is that PW 1 Sub-Inspector of Police Md Ibrahim attached to Motijheel Police Station, Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Dhaka, lodged a FIR with GRP Police Station, Dhaka on 10-4-2005 at about 21-20 pm alleging inter-alia, that, on 9-4-2005 at about 18-05 pm when he rushed to the Shahjahanpur Police Petrol with his forces received an wireless message and found one Anwar Hossain detained by people. Anwar Hossain showed them a decapitated head of a young boy. On interrogation, he told them that for the purpose of extorting money from the owner of Mukta Tailors he along with Zakir and others took a boy of 8/10 years old from Kamlapur Railway Station to Gazipur Shalban Forest and killed that boy and then decapitated his head from body and returned to Kamlapur Railway Station. But local people out of suspicion detained him and handed over to Shahjahanpur Police Station. Hence the case. 

 5. The Investigating Officer investigated the case. During investigation he visited the place of occurrences, prepared the sketch maps, index, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code, arrested accused Zakir from Hazigonj Police Station, Chandpur. Accused Jakir and Anwar @ Shankar made judicial confessions under section 164 of the Code which were recorded by competent Magistrates. On completion of investigation Investigating Officer of the case submitted charge sheet against Md Anwar Hossain @ Shankar Chandra Debnath and Md Zakir Hossain @ Zakir under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 7. Prosecution examined only 6(six) witnesses out of 39(thirty nine) witnesses of charge sheet. After closing the prosecution case condemned-prisoner-appellants were examined under section 342 of the Code to which they repeated their innocence. 

 8. Defence case as it appears from the trend of cross examination of the PW's and the suggestions put forwarded to them is the total denial of the case and they have been falsely implicated in this case. Accused Anwar @ Sankar's specific case is that the head of the victim was cut down in rail line and accused Anwar Hossain went to see that occurrence and from there he was apprehended and falsely been entangled with the case. 

 9. The learned Judge of the Trial Court thereafter in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case found condemned-prisoners guilty and convicted and sentenced as aforesaid. 

 14. After 8 years, on 24-2-2016 PW 1 Sub-Inspector of Police Gazi Md Ibrahim was cross examined by defence. In cross examination he staled that local people took Anwar @ Sankar to Shahjahanpur Police Fari. He came and saw that many people were staying there. He also saw accused Anwar@ Sankar was there with a decapitated head of a boy. He further stated that he arrested accused Anwar and then went to Gazipur. He tried to arrest Zakir. He stated that it is not a fact that the head of the victim was cut down in rail line and accused Anwar@ Sankar went to see the occurrence but the prosecution falsely implicated him in this case. 

 22. Mr Shaheen Ahmed khan, learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr SM Ashraful Hogue (George), learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr Mehadi Hasan (Milon), learned Assistant Attorney-General with Mr Al Mamun, learned Assistant Attorney-General with Mr Md Hafizur Rahman, learned Assistant Attorney-General with Mr Md Faruk Hossain, learned Assistant Attorney-General & Ms. Farida Parvin Flora, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State and in support of the death reference. Upon placing the FIR, charge sheet, charge, depositions of the witnesses, the confessional statements of the accuseds under section 164 of the Code, Post-Mortem Report, impugned judgment and order including other connected materials on record Mr Shaheen Ahmed Khan, learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the learned Judge of the Trial Court rightly relied on the statements of the witnesses, particularly confessional statements of the accuseds (1) Md Anwar Hossain @ Shankar Chandra Debnath and (2) Md Zakir Hossain @ Zakir and other evidences arrived at a correct decision against the condemned-prisoners. He referred the case of State vs Jahedul Islam @ Moulavi Babu 14 BLC (AD) 105, Aziz @ Azizul @ Azid vs State 73 DLR (AD) 365, Dipak Kumar Sarkar vs the State 1988 BLD (AD) 109 = 40 DLR (AD) 139, Abdus Samad vs The State 16 DLR SC 261,15 DLR (SC) 261. 

 23. Mr Ahmed further submits that in this case Md Anwar Hossain @ Sankar Chandra Debnath confessed his guilt under section 164 of the Code which is true and voluntary and he himself pointed out the headless body of victim from Joydebpur Shalbon, .where Police recovered the headless body of that unknown boy. 

 24. On the other hand Mr Mohammad Shishir Manir, learned Advocate for the appellant appearing on behalf of condemned-prisoner Md Anwar Hossain @ Sankar submits that he is totally innocent and he has not committed the crime as alleged by the prosecution. He further submits that the impugned judgment is illegal and unwarranted by facts and circumstances of the case as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside. He referred the cases 2 CLR 358 The State vs Mst Rozvshan Ara Begum, 15 BLT (AD) 104 The State vs Mofizuddin, 8 ELT (AD) 87 The State vs Md Farid Khan, (2001) 4 SCC 09 Dhanajaya Redy vs State of Karnataka, 73 DLR 123 Banu vs Bangladesh, (2008) 3 CALLT 345 Md Selim Akhter vs The State of West Bengal, (1983) 4 SCC 141 Rudul Sah vs State of Bihar, Chapter 14 Modi's Book on Medical Jurisprudence. 

 25. Mr SM Mahbubul Islam, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of condemned-prisoner Md Zakir Hossain @ Zakir submits that he should be acquitted on setting aside the order of conviction & sentence passed against him by the learned Judge of the trial Court in consideration of the facts that there is no independent witnesses in the case, the trial court misinterpreted, misread and misunderstood the evidences as well as the so-called confessional statement of the accused as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside. 

 26. In this case condemned-prisoner Anwar @ Sankar and Jakir made confessional statements before Magistrate, 1st Class under. section 164 of the Code. To have a better view of the matter, we would like to quote the statements of them which read as under:— 

 27. Now, in view of the submissions and counter submissions of the learned DAG for the prosecution, learned Advocates for the appellant Anwar @ Sankar and Zakir Hossain @ Jakir as above, let us review the relevant evidences and materials on record and scan the attending circumstances of the case to arrive at a correct decision as to whether the learned Judge of the trial Court was justified or not in passing the impugned judgment and order of sentence. 

 29. Secondly, as per prosecution case a decapitated head of an unknown boy of about 8/10 years old was recovered from condemned-prisoner Anwar @ Sankars' possession on 9-4-2005 at about 6-00 pm. But only PW 1 Gazi Ibrahim a Police Officer stated it. None of the witnesses including public and accompanied Police persons supported this statement. Only PW 2 Md Shahin Mia stated that in his presence seizure-list of that decapitated head was prepared. But he did not say a single word that this head was recovered from condemned-prisoner Anwar @ Sankar's possession as per prosecution story. 

 32. Lastly, in this case, out of 39 charge sheeted witnesses only 6 persons came to depose. All of them are formal witnesses. Among 39 witnesses 19 witnesses are from Police Department. But without PW 1 none of a single Police person came to corroborate the statement of PW 1. Furthermore that PW 1 a Police person came to the Court after 8 years to face the cross-examination. It appears that all of them played a hide and seek game to prove the murder of an unfortunate unknown boy of 8/10 years old. Thus, a copy of this judgment be sent to the Inspector General of Police of Bangladesh for taking necessary action against all of the charge sheeted Police persons that why not a single Police Officer came to depose in this case to corroborate PW l's statement. 

 33. It appears from the record that condemned-prisoner Anwar @ Sankar and Md Zakir Hossain have been languishing in Jail custody since their arrest i.e 16 years back, of which about 6 years they have been kept in condemned cell. No doubt this type of case in our hand where the condemned-prisoners Anwar @ Sankar and Zakir Hossain became victims of miscarriage of justice and we think it's a proper case to seek for an order of compensation/proper rehabilitation from proper forum. 

 34. Considering the facts and circumstances and evidences on record, this Court finds that there is absolutely no legal & trustworthy evidence against the condemned-prisoners to implicate them with the so-called murder of an unknown person and any conviction in case of a dearth of such evidence shall be unjustified and unwarranted. 

 39. Accordingly, let the condemned-prisoner-appellants (1) Md Anowar Hossain @ Md Rajib @ Golam Rabbani @ Shankar Chandra Debnath and (2) Md Zakir Hossain be set at liberty at once if they are not wanted in connection with any other case.
